sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Troy, New York?
sections.html:
You can hire an agent, sell without one, or accept an offer from a cash buyer. In Troy, all three end with a deed, a transfer tax return, and recording at the Rensselaer County Clerk, so the real decision is about speed, condition and how much work you want to take on.

An agent listing works best for a house that is move-in ready, since buyers who need a mortgage will order an appraisal and an inspection. A direct cash sale is more common for houses with deferred repairs, tenant issues, code questions or an estate behind them. Whatever the condition, have your tax bill, any lease and any repair receipts ready for a buyer.

  • List it: broadest audience, plus repairs, showings and a lender-driven closing.
  • Sell it yourself: no commission, but you handle every contract and negotiation.
  • Cash offer: the buyer purchases the house as it is and you choose the closing date.

Compare offers by what you would walk away with after the tax bill, any liens and the transfer tax, not by the price on the first page.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Troy for a seller?
sections.html:
Troy is the seat of Rensselaer County, on the east bank of the Hudson River just northeast of Albany. The Census Bureau estimates 50,912 residents as of July 1, 2025, down 0.7 percent from the 2020 base, on 10.36 square miles of land.

The city was named Troy in 1789, chartered in 1816, and later became known as the Collar City because its factories made most of the detachable collars worn in America around the turn of the 20th century. Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute opened in 1824, Emma Willard founded her school in 1821, and Russell Sage College and Hudson Valley Community College are here too. All of them are within the city limits.

The land runs flat along the river and climbs steeply toward the east, up to about 500 feet. The northern end was once the separate city of Lansingburgh, and the Poesten Kill and Wynants Kill cut through town on their way to the Hudson. On a sloped lot, buyers may ask how water drains away from the house, so have any answers ready.

Getting around runs on US 4 along River Street, NY 7 on Hoosick Street, NY 2 on Congress Street and the end of Interstate 787. CDTA buses connect Troy with Albany, Cohoes, Waterford and Watervliet. Two public school districts serve the city, Troy and Lansingburgh, and the one that applies to your street affects your school tax bill.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Troy housing?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024, the median value of an owner-occupied home in Troy is $206,500, and only 37.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $1,175, and the city has 21,265 households.

That ownership rate is lower than in most upstate suburbs, and it points to a market with many landlords and small investors. If your house has two or three units, expect buyers to ask for rent rolls, leases and utility costs. Median household income is $58,477 and 23.4 percent of residents are in poverty, so price your house against close comparables rather than a citywide figure.

Climate is a factor in older buildings. Troy has a humid continental climate with a January average near 25.5 degrees and about 42 inches of precipitation a year, so be ready to show the age of your roof and heating system.

sections.h2: How does Troy assess and bill property taxes?
sections.html:
The City Assessor's Office values about 13,400 properties each year and last revalued the city in 2013, according to the assessor page. A 2013 revaluation means assessments can sit well away from today's market prices, so do not assume your assessed value predicts your sale price.

Troy assessment and billing dates from city pages
DateWhat happens
March 1Taxable status date and exemption filing deadline
May 1Tentative roll filed and change of assessment notices mailed
Fourth Tuesday in MayGrievance Day, when the Board of Assessment Review hears complaints
July 1Final roll filed, the basis for school, city and county taxes
January and JulyCity and county tax installments due

School taxes are billed separately for the Troy and Lansingburgh districts, and the city's tax bill page says penalties on them accrue monthly after the due date. For a balance, call the Treasurer's Office at 518-279-7115. A bill copy is free to the owner and costs $5 for anyone else.

A buyer who wants an estimate of taxes without exemptions can ask the Assessor's Office, which is a useful step to take early if you are preparing a listing.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and deadlines affect a Troy owner this winter?
sections.html:
The city's exemptions page says renewal packets for the senior and disability-with-limited-income exemptions went out in October 2026 and must be returned before March 1, 2027. The income limit for Rensselaer County and the City of Troy is $48,399, based on 2025 household income.

  • STAR: new applicants register with the NYS Tax Department rather than the city.
  • Seniors and disabled owners: file the renewal with a copy of your 2025 federal tax return, or an income worksheet if you do not file.
  • Veterans: the city lists the RP-458-a alternative and RP-458-b Cold War applications.
  • First-time buyers of newly constructed homes, capital improvements and historic rehabilitation have their own forms.

An exemption does not move to the buyer. A buyer applies on their own after buying, which is one reason a bill can rise after a sale. If you hold a senior exemption, tell the buyer's side that the figure on your bill will not be the figure they pay.

sections.h2: What do Troy's code enforcement rules mean for a sale?
sections.html:
The Bureau of Code Enforcement issues building permits, runs housing and construction inspections, inspects vacant buildings and issues certificates of occupancy and compliance, according to the city's Code Enforcement page. The city adopted an updated zoning ordinance and use maps in April 2023, which matters if you plan to describe the property as a legal two-family or mixed use.

Before you list, ask Code Enforcement at 518-279-7180 whether any open violations, vacant building requirements or certificate questions are attached to your address. A cash buyer will usually take a house with defects, but unresolved city paperwork can still delay a closing.

If the building has been vacant, check with the bureau about vacant building inspection rules before you accept an offer, so you do not hand a buyer a surprise.

faqs.a: Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25 in 2027. The tentative roll is filed May 1 and the Board of Assessment Review hears complaints that day.

faqs.q: When are Troy city and county taxes due?
faqs.a: They are payable in two installments, the first due in January and the second in July. School taxes are billed separately by the Troy or Lansingburgh district, and the Treasurer's Office at 518-279-7115 can answer questions about your bill.

faqs.q: Who pays the New York transfer tax in Troy?
faqs.a: The seller pays the base tax of $2 for each $500 of consideration. The TP-584 return is filed with the county clerk and is due within 15 days after the deed is delivered. A buyer pays the 1 percent additional tax only on residences of $1 million or more.

faqs.q: Will my senior exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Exemptions are tied to the owner who qualifies, so the buyer files their own applications by the March 1 deadline. Expect the buyer's tax bill to differ from yours.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Troy house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, but contact the Bureau of Code Enforcement first to see what is open at your address. A cash buyer can take a house in rough shape, and open city items still need an owner's attention before or at closing.
